topic.coverageNote: Open paper that names hydroxyapatite among basic calcium phosphate crystals and links them to osteoarthritis, calcific tendinitis, acute arthritis, and Milwaukee shoulder. A rotator-cuff calcific-tendinopathy review did not use the word hydroxyapatite and was not the primary source.

mcqs.question: Which crystals does this paper group with hydroxyapatite in basic calcium phosphate disease?

options.A: Carbonated apatite, octacalcium phosphate, tricalcium phosphate, and whitlockite

mcqs.explanation: The paper lists carbonated apatite, hydroxyapatite, octacalcium phosphate, tricalcium phosphate, and whitlockite together.

sourceRefs.excerpt: crystals including carbonated-apatite (CA), hydroxyapatite (HA), octacalcium phosphate (OCP), tricalcium phosphate and whitlockite

mcqs.question: With which clinical conditions does the paper associate these crystals?

options.A: Osteoarthritis, calcific tendinitis, acute arthritis, and atherosclerosis

mcqs.explanation: The paper says these crystals are associated with osteoarthritis, calcific tendinitis, acute arthritis, and atherosclerosis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: are associated with osteoarthritis (OA), calcific tendinitis, acute arthritis and atherosclerosis

mcqs.question: Which syndrome does the paper use to illustrate BCP crystals in rapidly destructive osteoarthritis?
mcqs.explanation: The paper says the crystals are identified in synovial fluid of rapidly destructive OA, as illustrated by Milwaukee shoulder syndrome.

sourceRefs.excerpt: They are identified in the synovial fluid of rapidly destructive OA, as illustrated by the Milwaukee shoulder syndrome

mcqs.question: What alternative interpretation of articular BCP crystals does the paper say some investigators still hold?

options.A: They are innocent bystanders or markers of end-stage osteoarthritis

mcqs.explanation: The paper says some investigators still consider articular BCP crystals innocent bystanders and/or markers of end-stage OA.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Some investigators still consider articular BCP crystals as “innocent bystanders” and/or markers of end-stage OA.

mcqs.question: Where else does the paper say these crystals are highly prevalent?

options.A: Cartilage from osteoarthritic knees at joint replacement
options.C: Only the vitreous of the eye

mcqs.explanation: The paper says they are also highly prevalent in cartilage from affected OA joints at knee replacement.

sourceRefs.excerpt: highly prevalent in cartilage obtained from affected OA joints at the time of knee joint replacement surgery
